paragraphs.title: The Request of Gad and Reuben

easy.explanation: Numbers 32:1 says that Reuben and Gad had a very great multitude of cattle.
easy.q: Which two tribes had a very great multitude of cattle?

answers: The land of Jazer and the land of Gilead
easy.explanation: They saw that Jazer and Gilead were places for cattle.
easy.q: Which lands did the children of Gad and Reuben see as suitable for cattle?

answers: Permission to remain in the wilderness
The land east of Jordan as a possession
easy.explanation: They asked for the land as a possession and asked not to be brought over Jordan.
easy.q: What did Gad and Reuben ask Moses to give them?

answers: It was suitable for their cattle
medium.explanation: The passage says the land was a place for cattle, and the tribes had many cattle.
medium.q: Why did Gad and Reuben want the land of Jazer and Gilead?

answers: An inheritance or portion of land
medium.explanation: A possession is land given to someone as an inheritance.
medium.q: In this passage, what does “possession” mean?

answers: They sought approval from the leaders of Israel
medium.explanation: They presented their request before the recognized leaders of the congregation.
medium.q: What does their speaking to Moses, Eleazar, and the princes show?

answers: Their cattle led them to choose land suited for grazing
Their cattle prevented them from settling
Their cattle required them to cross Jordan
challenge.explanation: They wanted the region because it was suitable for their large herds.
challenge.q: How were the tribes’ possessions connected with their request for land?

answers: They wanted to go before all the people
They did not want an inheritance
They wanted to remain east of Jordan
challenge.explanation: Their request was to receive an inheritance on the eastern side of Jordan.
challenge.q: What can be understood from the words “bring us not over Jordan”?

answers: They made a request, found the land, and then saw their cattle
They had many cattle, identified suitable land, and requested it
They requested land, fought a battle, and then found the land
challenge.explanation: The passage first mentions their cattle, then the suitable land, and finally their request.
challenge.q: What is the logical order of events in these verses?

paragraphs.title: Moses’ Fear of Repeating the Spies’ Sin

answers: Discourage the heart of the children of Israel
easy.explanation: Moses feared their decision would discourage Israel from entering the land.
easy.q: What did Moses fear that Gad and Reuben would do?

easy.explanation: Moses referred to what their fathers did when the spies viewed the land.
easy.q: Whom did Moses compare their possible action to?

easy.explanation: Numbers 32:13 says that the LORD made Israel wander forty years.
easy.q: How many years did the Israelites wander in the wilderness?

answers: It could discourage Israel from entering the land
It would cause a shortage of cattle
It would prevent the building of cities
medium.explanation: Moses feared that the people would lose heart and refuse to enter the land given by the LORD.
medium.q: Why did Moses fear that their request would harm all Israel?

answers: To weaken someone’s courage or determination
medium.explanation: The expression means to cause the people to lose courage.
medium.q: In context, what does “discourage the heart” mean?

answers: Caleb the son of Jephunneh and Joshua the son of Nun
medium.explanation: The passage specifically names Caleb and Joshua.
medium.q: Which two men had wholly followed the LORD?

answers: Both could discourage the heart of the people
challenge.explanation: Moses feared that the tribes’ decision would produce the same discouragement caused by the spies.
challenge.q: What connection did Moses make between the tribes’ decision and the spies’ sin?

answers: Their actions could harm the whole nation
They would lose only their cattle
They would have to build a wall
challenge.explanation: Moses viewed their decision as something that could negatively affect all Israel.
challenge.q: What does Moses’ warning about destroying the people imply?

answers: That generation did evil in the sight of the LORD
The tribe of Manasseh made a request
challenge.explanation: The wandering was connected with the sin of the generation that did evil before the LORD.
challenge.q: According to the passage, why did Israel wander in the wilderness?

paragraphs.title: The Pledge to Join the War

easy.explanation: They said, “We will build sheepfolds here for our cattle.”
easy.q: What did Gad and Reuben say they would build for their cattle?

easy.explanation: The men promised to go ready armed before Israel.
easy.q: Who would go before the children of Israel to war?

answers: Until all Israel had inherited its inheritance
easy.explanation: They would not return home until every Israelite had received an inheritance.
easy.q: How long would they remain with Israel in the war?

answers: To protect them from the inhabitants of the land
To keep them away from the cattle
medium.explanation: The passage says the families would dwell in fenced cities because of the inhabitants of the land.
medium.q: Why would their little ones dwell in fenced cities?

medium.explanation: The phrase describes armed men going out to fight.
medium.q: What does “go ready armed” mean in this context?

answers: A desire to avoid every battle
medium.explanation: They tied their return home to the completion of Israel’s inheritance.
medium.q: What did the tribes show by refusing to return home until Israel received its inheritance?

answers: They promised that their armed men would go before Israel
They promised not to build cities
They promised to sell their cattle
challenge.explanation: They assured Moses that their men would go before Israel and would not abandon their brethren.
challenge.q: How did Gad and Reuben answer Moses’ concern?

answers: Receiving land did not remove their duty to fight
Receiving land canceled their duty to fight
Only the families had to fight
challenge.explanation: Although they requested land, they promised to fight until all Israel received its inheritance.
challenge.q: What does their pledge show about the relationship between receiving land and responsibility?

answers: War, building cities, and then leaving their families
Building towns and sheepfolds, sending the men to war, and returning afterward
Returning home, going to war, and then building sheepfolds
challenge.explanation: They would prepare homes and sheepfolds, fight with Israel, and return after the inheritance was secured.
challenge.q: What was the order of their plan?

answers: The armed men must go before the LORD to war
The tribes must abandon their cattle
easy.explanation: Moses required the men to go armed before the LORD in battle.

answers: They would be guiltless before the LORD and Israel
They would remain in the wilderness
easy.explanation: Moses said they would be guiltless before the LORD and before Israel.
easy.q: What would happen if Gad and Reuben fulfilled their promise?

answers: Pass armed before the LORD into Canaan
easy.explanation: They promised to pass armed before the LORD into the land of Canaan.
easy.q: What did Gad and Reuben promise to do?

answers: They would fail to keep their word
medium.explanation: Moses treated failure to perform their promise as sin against the LORD.
medium.q: Why would failure to keep the condition be sin against the LORD?

medium.explanation: Here, guiltless means free from blame before the LORD and Israel.
medium.q: What does “guiltless” mean in “ye shall be guiltless”?

answers: Cities for their little ones and folds for their sheep
medium.explanation: Moses instructed them to build cities for their little ones and folds for their sheep.
medium.q: What did Moses tell them to build for their families and cattle?

answers: Their promise involved both religious and national responsibility
Israel would not participate in the war
challenge.explanation: Breaking the promise would violate their duty to the LORD and to the nation.
challenge.q: Why did Moses mention both the LORD and Israel?

answers: They must carry out what they promised
They must speak with the spies
challenge.explanation: Moses required them to fulfill the commitment they had spoken.
challenge.q: What does “do that which hath proceeded out of your mouth” mean?

answers: Moses set a condition, and they accepted it
Moses rejected the request, and they left
The tribes gave Moses a new condition
challenge.explanation: They answered that they would do as Moses commanded.
challenge.q: What was the relationship between Moses’ condition and the tribes’ response?

paragraphs.title: Entrusting the Agreement and Assigning the Land

answers: Eleazar, Joshua, and the chief fathers of the tribes
easy.explanation: Moses commanded Eleazar, Joshua, and the chief fathers concerning the arrangement.
easy.q: Upon whom did Moses place responsibility for the agreement?

answers: Gad, Reuben, and half the tribe of Manasseh
easy.explanation: Moses gave the territory to Gad, Reuben, and half of Manasseh.
easy.q: To whom were the lands of Sihon and Og given?

answers: They had to pass armed to war with Israel
They had to give up their cattle
They had to remain in the wilderness
easy.explanation: Their possession depended on passing over armed and helping subdue the land.
easy.q: What was required for them to receive the land of Gilead?

answers: They would receive possessions among Israel in Canaan
They would be left without families
medium.explanation: Moses said they would have possessions among the other tribes in Canaan.
medium.q: What would happen if Gad and Reuben did not pass over armed?

medium.explanation: The word refers to men equipped and prepared for battle.
medium.q: What does “armed” or “armed to battle” describe here?

answers: Moses gave that half-tribe a portion of the land
It did not participate in the war
medium.explanation: The passage explicitly says that Moses gave land to half the tribe of Manasseh.
medium.q: Why was half of Manasseh included in the division?

answers: The agreement was public, binding, and supervised
The agreement was a private secret
challenge.explanation: The involvement of the leaders gave the arrangement public authority and oversight.
challenge.q: What does placing the agreement in the care of the leaders show?

answers: By fulfilling their promise to help conquer the land
Only by the size of their herds
challenge.explanation: Their inheritance was connected with passing over armed and helping Israel.
challenge.q: How was the tribes’ right to the land east of Jordan established?

answers: The condition, the result if fulfilled, and the result if not fulfilled
Punishment, request, and division of cattle
Building towns, returning home, and then fighting
challenge.explanation: Moses first states the condition, then explains the outcome of obedience and failure.
challenge.q: What is the structure of Moses’ instruction?

paragraphs.title: Building the Towns of Gad and Reuben and the Conquests of Manasseh

easy.explanation: The children of Gad and Reuben built and fortified towns and made sheepfolds.
easy.q: Which tribes built towns and sheepfolds east of Jordan?

answers: The children of Machir the son of Manasseh
easy.explanation: The children of Machir went to Gilead and took it.
The passage says that Nobah took Kenath and its villages.
easy.q: Who captured Kenath and its villages?

medium.explanation: Beth-nimrah and Beth-haran are described as fenced cities, with folds for sheep.
medium.q: What was the character of some of the towns built by Gad?

answers: The names of some towns were changed
medium.explanation: The verse states that some of the towns received other names.
medium.q: What does “their names being changed” mean?

answers: He took the small towns and called them Havoth-jair
He left the land of Manasseh
medium.explanation: Jair captured the small towns and named them Havoth-jair.
medium.q: What did Jair do after the Manassites took Gilead?

answers: The new settlers wished to establish new names for the towns
The tribes gave up the land
challenge.explanation: The passage says that other names were given to the towns they built or occupied.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the changing of the towns’ names?

answers: They captured and developed the region given to them
challenge.explanation: The Manassites took Gilead and its settlements and then dwelt there.
challenge.q: How were the actions of Manasseh connected with the inheritance they received?

answers: Gad and Reuben built towns, while Manasseh captured regions and settlements
Gad and Reuben captured the land, while Manasseh built only sheepfolds
challenge.explanation: The verses emphasize construction by Gad and Reuben and conquest by the Manassites.
challenge.q: What difference appears between the actions of Gad and Reuben and those of Manasseh?
